correctness.rationale: The universal argument treats every finite irreducible rational 2-by-2 semigroup. The 0-minimal ideal is completely 0-simple, its nonzero rank is either one or two, and a local rank-one scalar group lies in {+1,-1}. Normalized Rees row/column vectors have signed 0/1 pairings; irreducibility forces their spans to be two-dimensional. The signed rank-two incidence lemma proves ab<=9, and any rank-one map outside the ideal must be a signed normalized outer product. Full-rank members form a finite rational subgroup of order at most 12, giving 1+18+12=31. The explicit 31-element construction is closed and irreducible; a fully exact checker confirms 961 products and independently enumerates all possible signed-incidence directions. No finite check substitutes for the symbolic structural proof.

value.rationale: Kiefer--Ryzhikov explicitly ask for exact largest irreducible matrix semigroups. This determines the first nontrivial dimensional value rather than providing another loose upper bound: 31 versus 81. The proof isolates a natural and sharp rank-two signed-incidence bottleneck, with a 12-unit/18-rank-one realization, giving a structural extremal result that is useful as a benchmark and a possible guide to higher-dimensional cases. It is not merely a routine numerical increment or an arbitrary computational slice.
